subject: Post-call: EdgeFin Performance SLO & Benchmark Methodology - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@edgefin.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps: Performance SLOs / benchmark methodology

Hi Alice / Tom 	6

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the benchmark run: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Target latency SLOs: p95 <= 150ms for first token (streaming enabled), p99 tail for full response <= 250ms for the 256-token gen profile.
- Throughput & concurrency: goal is sustained 300 QPS with spikes to 600 QPS; expected concurrency ~120 active connections during peak.
- Streaming: EdgeFin requires chunked streaming (server-sent events / chunked HTTP) for first-token and progressive tokens; client expects max per-chunk latency <= 50ms.
- Stability: 30-minute sustained window for throughput/latency characterization; warm-up run of 5 minutes recommended.

What we shared (attached / links)
- fineedge-benchmark-plan-v1.pdf 	6 proposed methodology, measurement definitions, and gating criteria.
- Eval harness link (shared Drive) with test runner and example scripts: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-eval-harness-link

Ask from EdgeFin (what we need from you)
1) Canonical prompt set & expected output variants (edge cases / long tail prompts).
2) Clarify streaming chunk semantics (preferred chunk size, whether partial tokens ok).
3) Confirm acceptable warm-up policy and if synthetic user patterns are representative.
4) Any constraints on test data residency or masking (PII).

Next steps / owners
- EdgeFin (Alice): Send prompt set + confirm streaming semantics by EOD 6/30.
- Rishi (solutions): We'll prepare a benchmark plan summary and runbook.
- Dev (infra): Schedule canary benchmark on our staging cluster; target window July 6, 9–11am PT (pending your availability).

I've attached the draft benchmark plan for your review (finedge-benchmark-plan-v1.pdf). Once we have the prompt set and streaming details we can finalize measurement windows and start the canary run.

Thanks 	6 looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: fineedge-benchmark-plan-v1.pdf

From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@edgefin.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps: Performance SLOs / benchmark methodology

Marissa 	6 thanks for the clear recap. Attaching our canonical prompt set and a short readme (edgefin-prompt-set-v1.json) 	6 covers the three primary workflows: short lookups, multi-turn chat, and long-form generation (~250–300 tokens).

Streaming specifics / clarifications:
- We require chunked streaming for first token: first-token latency ideally <150ms; subsequent chunks should arrive within 40–60ms.
- Chunk size: we prefer logical token chunks (not byte-size), but if you measure by bytes, target ~512–1024 bytes per chunk.
- Partial tokens: acceptable as long as we receive progressive output; client will reassemble.

Concurrency / load profile:
- Sustained target: 300 QPS across a pool of 120 concurrent clients.
- Burst capacity: up to 600 QPS for 30s–60s windows.

Privacy / data residency:
- Test prompts contain sanitized customer-like examples (no PII).
- We require test results to be stored for 30 days and then purged; please confirm similar retention on your side for benchmark logs.

We also included a small sample of expected output variants 	6 not strict pass/fail, but used for qualitative checks.

Let us know if the attached prompt set needs reformatting to plug into your harness. Happy to hop on a 15-min sync if that helps.

Regards,
Alice Zhang
Head of ML Engineering | EdgeFin
alice.zhang@edgefin.com
(212) 555-0178

Attachments: edgefin-prompt-set-v1.json

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps: Performance SLOs / benchmark methodology

Marissa / Dev 	6

Thanks Alice for the prompt set 	6 looks comprehensive. A couple of notes from the engineering/runbook side before we lock the canary window: 

Measurement definitions (proposed):
- Latency: measure server-observed first-byte and last-byte times. Report p50/p95/p99 for both first-byte (TTFB) and end-to-end response.
- Throughput: measured as completed responses/sec over a 30-minute steady-state window; separate short-burst windows (30–60s) for spike testing.
- Concurrency: map QPS to client connections in the harness (we'll emulate 120 clients at a mix of 60% short-lookup, 30% chat, 10% long-form).
- Warm-up: 5 minutes of incremental ramp to target to populate KV caches / model caches.
- Reproducibility: we'll run three independent trials and provide median and variance.

Infrastructure / practicals:
- Dev: Can we reserve the staging pool July 6, 9–11am PT? We'll need logs retained for 30 days per EdgeFin request and a downloadable CSV of measured metrics.
- We'll push a small patch to the harness to emit per-chunk timestamps for streaming checks (eval-harness-instructions.md attached).

Action items:
- Dev: schedule the staging cluster and confirm retention + access control for logs.
- Marissa: confirm the canary window with EdgeFin (I'll stand by for run execution).

I'll kick off the harness pre-flight today and validate the runners with a short dry run.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com
